correctness.rationale: For 1<=a<=b and 1<=n<=a+b with possibly different monotone normalized valuations, prove three complementary ranges. For n<=a, Bei et al. Proposition 4.8 applies; n=1 is immediate. For n>=b, t=a+b-n<=a, after each agent chooses her best available singleton, the x leftover L vertices fit among b-y chosen R vertices and the y leftover R among a-x chosen L: both inequalities follow from t<=a<=b. Attach each leftover to a different opposite-side chosen singleton. Every bundle is a singleton or an edge, and each agent i may remove the chosen vertex of j, leaving a leftover that was available at i's pick, so even EF1_outer follows without additivity. For a<n<b, an R-only singleton is forced; unit additive envy implies every other bundle size<=2, at most a size-2 bundles, and n+a<a+b is a contradiction. Independently checked all residual cardinality inequalities in 36,769 cases; no finite check is used as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Low range invokes precisely the cited published connected ordinary EF1 theorem; outer EF1 is asserted only in high range.
